change_summary: The journal's editors issued an expression of concern for this paper, saying they were made aware of concerns about some of the data reported in it. The matter is still being looked into, and the notice does not say which data or figures are affected. Because the concern is about data and no outcome is given, the findings are in doubt but not shown to be wrong.
evaluation: Your Discussion cites [8] (Lopez and Chen) as showing reduced activity in recipient mice, supporting a causal role of gut bacteria in depressive behaviour. You also say your own proposal builds on this finding, and the paper's abstract reports that result from a forced-swim test (Figure 3). The editors say they have been made aware of concerns about some of the data in the article, but the notice does not say which data or figures are affected. So it is unclear whether the change touches your use of the paper, since the concern is about unspecified data and your claim relies on the Figure 3 result. Treating that uncertain use as affected, the impact on your Discussion is medium.
recommendation: Your Discussion cites [8] as showing reduced activity in recipient mice, supporting a causal role of gut bacteria, and says your own proposal builds on this finding. The editors say they were made aware of concerns about some of the data in the article, but the notice does not say which data or figures are affected. Hedge the causal wording, cite the notice, and avoid building new work on this finding for now. Check the journal's page for updates on which data are affected; if a retraction follows, a new alert would be raised.
